MINUTES
  PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING
  March 6, 2017

A regular meeting of the Planning Commission of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to
order at 7:00 p.m. in the City Hall Council Chambers, 4045 Palos Verdes Drive North, by
CHAIRMAN YOO.

2.  PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

CHAIRMAN YOO led the assembly in the Pledge of Allegiance to the Flag.

3.  ROLL CALL

Commissioners Present:  Thomas, Scott, Medawar, Carman, Schachter, Chair Yoo

Commissioners Absent:  Zigrang

Staff Present:  Planning Director Wahba, Associate Planner Thom, Planning
  Technician/Code Enforcement Administrator Slawson

4.  APPROVAL OF MINUTES

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to,

  APPROVE THE MINUTES OF THE REGULAR PLANNING COMMISSION MEETING OF
  FEBRUARY 6, 2017.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

5.  AUDIENCE ITEMS

None.

6.  CONSENT CALENDAR

  A. WAIVE READING IN FULL OF ALL RESOLUTIONS THAT ARE PRESENTED FOR THE
  CONSIDERATION OF THE PLANNING COMMISSION ON TONIGHT’S AGENDA AND
  ALL SUCH RESOLUTIONS SHALL BE READY BY TITLE ONLY.

  COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER,

  TO APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEM 6-A.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

7.  BUSINESS ITEMS

  A. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. PA-01-17; APPLICANT: MR. AND MRS. MASOOD
  ZAMAN; LOCATION: 5234 BLUEMOUND ROAD; A request for a Neighborhood
  Compatibility Determination to construct one and two-story additions to an existing one-
  story residence. Two Minor Deviation are requested, 1) for an increase of lot coverage by
  not more than 10% (38.5% max); and 2) for the encroachment of the proposed residence
  into the required front yard which does not project closer to the property line than the
  forward most building line. (KT)

Associate Planner Thom summarized the Staff Report (as per written material).

Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-01-17 with the conditions as provided in the Staff Report.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN requested confirmation on the changes to the second story windows.

Associate Planner Thom stated the windows are listed as a condition for approval in the staff
report. In addition, egress requirements are part of the Building & Safety plan check process.

  1
Planning Commission Minutes
March 6, 2017
 Jeff Lyon, Architect, 28 Pony Lane, RHE, stated that he added Ranch style architectural features
to the design. Mr. Lyon stated that he has discussed with his client that this project will take
approximately 6-8 months to complete. Mr. Lyon addressed the requirement for opaque windows
facing the west side on the second floor and stated that the windows do not compromise the
neighbor’s privacy.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if Mr. Lyon has considered a hip roof. Mr. Lyon stated that a
hip roof will not tie in with a Ranch style design and it would make for awkward roof lines.

Masood Zaman, Property Owner/Applicant, stated that his daughters grew up in this
neighborhood and their family would like to stay in this home. Mr. Zaman stated that he would
like the project to move forward quickly since there have been numerous delays.

Rachel Daly, 5235 Bluemound Rd., RHE, stated that the revised design for this project does not
adequately address the issues of mass and scale. She is also concerned with the amount of time
this project will take to complete. Ms. Daly also stated privacy concerns since her property is
directly across the street. Ms. Daly provided staff with notes detailing her concerns with the
subject property.

In response to a question from COMMISSIONER THOMAS, Jeff Lyon, Architect, responded
that the red trace in the plans was shown for the property that was closest and most affected by
the subject property. The other homes were quite a distance away.

Planning Director Wahba stated that staff considers the adequate distance rule when reviewing
similar projects. The neighbors closest to the subject property are considered.

Ms. Daly disagreed and stated that that she feels that her property is the most affected by this
project since her property faces directly in the direction of the subject property.

Planning Director Wahba explained the placement of the windows in the front elevation of the
home and stated that only the two bedroom windows facing the front would be used to look out
onto the street; the other two windows are (1) to a staircase landing and (2) to a bathroom which
will be opaque.

CHAIRMAN YOO asked if there is anywhere to move the location of the two bedroom windows
in the front of the property. Planning Director Wahba responded that placing them on the side
would not meet the minimum egress requirement.

COMMISSIONER THOMAS asked if the condition for an opaque window would satisfy the privacy
concern. COMMISSIONER SCOTT clarified that the window is to the staircase landing.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT stated that he does not recall a project challenged for privacy issues
from the neighbor across the street. Planning Director Wahba stated that the house is at least
80’ from home to home. In this case, the adequate distance rule would apply.

THE PLANNING COMMISSIONERS discussed the need to enforce the opacity requirement for
the window at the staircase and the number of comparable homes at the same size or larger
within this neighborhood.

COMMISSIONER CARMAN stated her concern with approving this project and setting a
precedent for similar projects.

Planning Director Wahba stated that from the 1960’s to 1980’s when the Neighborhood
Compatibility Determination was adopted, two-story homes were built and there were good and
bad cases. In the late 1990’s, the City Council adopted a policy stating that homes in this
neighborhood could not exceed 3,000 sq. ft. Planning Director Wahba provided additional
background on similar projects.

Lori Hathaway, 5227 Bluemound Rd., stated that another house on the street built a two-story
house and upon visiting the house found that they have a window that can look down into her
home and also stated that they do not have a view of the ocean or the city. Ms. Hathaway stated
that they may not accomplish obtaining a view as is sometimes assumed when building a second
floor.

Ms. Daly stated that staff told her that she could not build a second story since it would affect
neighboring views which causes an imbalance on the street.

  2
Planning Commission Minutes
March 6, 2017
 Planning Director Wahba stated that the in early to mid-90’s, the City Council and the Planning
Commission held a workshop to consider remodels in the Rollingwood neighborhood. At the
meeting it was determined that if a property owner remodels their home and acquires a view, it is
not a protected view. Typically the homes on the south side of the street are set higher and have
views between the houses.

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR,

  TO APPROVE PA-01-17 WITH CONDITIONS AS STATED IN THE STAFF REPORT
  WITH THE EXCEPTION OF THE WINDOW AT THE STAIRWAY LANDING WHICH IS

  NOT REQUIRED TO BE OPAQUE; THE BATHROOM WINDOW WILL BE REQUIRED
  TO BE OPAQUE AS STATED IN THE CONDITIONS FOR APPROVAL.

  AYES:  Thomas, Scott, Schachter, Medawar, Chair Yoo
  NOES:  Carman
  ABSENT:  Zigrang
  ABSTAIN

Planning Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission has approved Planning
Application No. 01-17. There is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

  B. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 02-17; APPLICANT: SCOTT DARNELL, ON BEHALF OF
  SRE DCM PV, LLC; LOCATION: 27520HAWTHORNE BLVD. (PENINSULA POINTE); An
  amendment to Planning Application 18-15 (City Council Resolution No. 2374).
  Modification of the Conditional Use Permit to allow 1,845 SF of medical office use and
  reduction of Assisted Living Units from 89 to 84;modification of the Precise Plan of Design
  for changes to surface stall parking arrangement and outdoor recreation areas; and
  amendment of a Variance to allow two additional parking stalls in the side setback area.
  (JN)
  NOTE: Staff is recommending to continue this item to the Planning Commission meeting
  scheduled on Monday, April 3, 2017 in order to provide sufficient time for the completion
  to prepare an addendum, which will address the proposed changes to the project.
  Associate Planner Thom summarized the Staff Report (as per written material).

  COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER MEDAWAR to,

  CONTINUE THIS ITEM TO THE PLANING COMMISSION MEETING OF APRIL 3, 2017.

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

Planning Commissioner Wahba stated that Planning Application No. 02-17 has been continued
to the meeting of April 3, 2017. There will be no further noticing of this item since it is continued
to a date certain.

  C. PLANNING APPLICATION NO. 05-17; APPLICANT: MR. AND MRS. VANDORDAKLOU;
  LOCATION: 3552 LARIAT LANE; A request for approval of a Neighborhood Compatibility
  Determination for a one and two-story additions to a single-story residence.

Associate Planner Thom summarized the Staff Report (as per written material).

Associate Planner Thom stated that staff recommends that the Planning Commission approve
PA-05-17 with the condition as provided in the Staff Report.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the square footage of the home compared to the comparable
property included the garage and other structures. Associate Planner Thom responded that only
livable space was used to compare the subject property size with other homes in the area and
confirmed that this is the smaller of the comparison.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if there are any view impacts. Planning Director Wahba stated
that there were no impacts to views that staff could identify.

CHAIRMAN YOO asked about scale and asked if the plate height could be reduced further.
Associate Planner Thom stated that the plate height could be reduced further particularly on the
first floor. Planning Director Wahba provided some background on plate heights.

  3
Planning Commission Minutes
March 6, 2017
 The PLANNING COMMISSION asked if staff will work with the applicant regarding the changes
that will need to be made prior to approval. Planning Director Wahba stated that staff will work
with the applicant to meet staff’s recommendation and if it is unresolved, the item will be brought
back before the Planning Commission for further review.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER THOMAS to,

  APPROVE PA-05-17 WITH THE CONDITIONS OF APPROVAL,

  AYES:  Thomas, Scott, Schachter, Carman, Medawar, Chair Yoo
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Zigrang
  ABSTAIN:

Planning Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission has approved PA-05-17. There
is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

8.  PUBLIC HEARINGS

  A. RESOLUTION NO. PA-04-17, Planning Commission to approve a Conditional Use Permit
  for a beer and wine license, which is incidental to the Inka Wasi restaurant relocation to
  the former Taco Bell restaurant space. APPLICATION: Inka Wasi; LOCATION: 5
  Peninsula Center.

Planning Technician/Code Enforcement Administrator Slawson summarized the Staff Report (as
per written material).

Planning Technician/Code Enforcement Administrator Slawson stated that staff recommends that
the Planning Commission open the public hearing, take public testimony, discuss the issues,
close the public hearing, and approve Planning Commission Resolution No. PA-04-17.

COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER asked if there would be any grounds for denying the application.
Planning Technician/Code Enforcement Administrator Slawson stated that there were no
comments from the public and the applicant had a beer and wine license at their former location
under a different name. The new location was the former Taco Bell site and there was no beer
and wine license approved for the site; in order for ABC to approve beer and wine, a Conditional
Use Permit is required.

Planning Director Wahba added that for beer and wine permits, ABC will require that there is a
condition that the alcohol be served, controlling alcohol in the outdoor area, and that it is incidental
to a restaurant.

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to

  OPEN THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER SCOTT to

  CLOSE THE PUBLIC HEARING

  There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered

  COMMISSIONER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by CHAIRMAN YOO to

  APPROVE THE CONDITIONAL USE PERMIT PA-04-17 FOR A BEER AND WINE
  LICENSE

  AYES:  Thomas, Scott, Schachter, Carman, Medawar, Chair Yoo
  NOES:
  ABSENT:  Zigrang
  ABSTAIN:

Planning Director Wahba stated that the Planning Commission has approved Resolution No. PA-
04-17. There is a 20-day appeal period for this item.

  4
Planning Commission Minutes
March 6, 2017
 Jeff Axtell, Vestar, stated that the friends and family opening was tonight and there will be a public
grand opening on the weekend of March 25th. On March 24th, there will be a “chainsaw” cutting
ceremony. Planning Director Wahba stated that the event will begin at 5:30 pm. The Chamber
of Commerce and City Council will be there and welcomed the Planning Commission to attend
as well.

COMMISSIONER SCOTT thanked Mr. Axtell for his hard work and great vision with revitalizing
the shopping center. Mr. Axtell stated that it has been a great partnership with the City and hopes
to open additional businesses.

9.  COMMISSION ITEMS

COMMISSIONER SCOTT asked if the Mendelson’s appealed. Planning Director Wahba stated
that they did and the item will be going before the City Council on March 28th. COMMISSIONER
SCOTT asked for a report on the position that the City Council takes on this item.

10.  DIRECTOR ITEMS

None

11.  MATTERS OF INFORMATION

  A. CITY COUNCIL ACTIONS OF JANUARY 24, 2017

  B. DRAFT PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES (1/17/17)

  C. DRAFT PARKS AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MEETING MINUTES (12/19/16)

COMMISSIONER SCOTT moved, seconded by COMMISSIONER THOMAS to,

  RECEIVE AND FILE ITEMS 12-A THROUGH 12-C.

There being no objection, CHAIRMAN YOO so ordered.

12.  ADJOURNMENT

CHAIRMAN YOO adjourned the meeting at 8:25 p.m. to the next Planning Commission meeting
of April 3, 2017.

Minutes Secretary  City Clerk
